$comment: THE ONE DECLARATION OF WHAT A FLASHABLE STORE HUB IMAGE CONTAINS.
It exists because the repository had two build paths that disagreed, and
nothing reconciled them. `scripts/profiles/store-hub.sh` defined a Hub agent
unit, but it is sourced only by `build-image.sh`, which refuses to emit an
.img. The real builder, `build-rpi-image.sh`, never sourced it. So the Hub
agent existed in the build path that cannot produce a card, and was absent
from the one that can -- while the image still advertised _kitluy-edge._tcp
on 7443. The Pi advertised a service that could not exist.
Three consumers read this file, which is what keeps them from drifting:
1. scripts/package-bootstrap-runtime.sh -- packages what is declared here
2. test/image-contents.test.sh          -- inspects a BUILT rootfs for it
3. test/systemd-runtime.test.sh         -- cross-checks enablement
Adding a component to the image means adding it HERE. A component declared
and not packaged fails the build; a component packaged and not declared is
invisible to the tests, which is the failure mode this file removes.
NOTHING PER-DEVICE BELONGS IN AN IMAGE. No device key, certificate, tenant,
store, location, staff record, machine-id or SSH host key is declared here,
and test/systemd-runtime.test.sh asserts their absence independently.
THE STORE HUB ITSELF: the LAN /edge/v1 API on 7443, local authority,
sync. Absent from every flashable image before BRINGUP-003 -- the
defect this manifest exists to make impossible.
`kind: bundle` and not `closure` because this package has 16 workspace
dependencies plus `pg`, and the image ships no node_modules. esbuild
resolves the graph at build time into one file.
